context.title: Riot in Ephesus
context.summary: In Ephesus Paul baptizes disciples of John, teaches for two years, and God works unusual miracles. Magic books are burned. Silversmiths who make shrines of the goddess Diana start a riot, which the town clerk calms.
context.background: Ephesus was a leading city of the province of Asia and home to the great temple of Artemis (called Diana in the KJV), one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world. The city was also famous for magic. Its huge open-air theater, where the crowd gathered, can still be seen.

customs.note: Likely drachmas, each about a day's wage, an enormous sum showing how seriously the converts broke with magic.
Small models of the goddess's shrine sold to pilgrims and worshipers. Fewer customers meant lost income.

watchFor: 'So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed' (v. 20).
The crowd shouts 'Great is Diana of the Ephesians' for about two hours (v. 34).

people.name: Paul
people.summary: Saul was born about the same time as our Lord. His circumcision-name was Saul, and probably the name Paul was also given to him in infancy “for use in the Gentile world,” as “Saul” would be his Hebrew home-name.

people.name: Apollos
people.summary: A Jew “born at Alexandria,” a man well versed in the Scriptures and eloquent (Acts 18:24; R.V., “learned”). He came to Ephesus (about A.D. 49), where he spake “boldly” in the synagogue (18:26), although he did not know as yet that Jesus of Nazareth was the Messiah.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: John
people.summary: The “forerunner of our Lord.” We have but fragmentary and imperfect accounts of him in the Gospels. He was of priestly descent.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Tyrannus
people.summary: Prince, a Greek rhetorician, in whose “school” at Ephesus Paul disputed daily for the space of two years with those who came to him (Acts 19:9).

people.name: Sceva
people.summary: An implement, a Jew, chief of the priests at Ephesus (Acts 19:13-16); i.e., the head of one of the twenty-four courses of the house of Levi.

people.name: Timotheus
people.summary: Honouring God, a young disciple who was Paul’s companion in many of his journeyings. His mother, Eunice, and his grandmother, Lois, are mentioned as eminent for their piety (2 Tim. 1:5).

people.name: Erastus
people.summary: A companion of Paul at Ephesus, who was sent by him along with Timothy into Macedonia (Acts 19:22).

people.name: Diana
people.summary: So called by the Romans; called Artemis by the Greeks, the “great” goddess worshipped among heathen nations under various modifications. Her most noted temple was that at Ephesus.

people.name: Demetrius
people.summary: A silversmith at Ephesus, whose chief occupation was to make “silver shrines for Diana”, Acts 19:24, i.e., models either of the temple of Diana or of the statue of the goddess.

people.name: Aristarchus
people.summary: Best ruler, native of Thessalonica (Acts 20:4), a companion of Paul (Acts 19:29; 27:2).

people.name: Gaius
people.summary: A Macedonian, Paul’s fellow-traveller, and his host at Corinth when he wrote his Epistle to the Romans (16:23). He with his household were baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14).

people.name: Alexander
people.summary: A Jew of Ephesus who took a prominent part in the uproar raised there by the preaching of Paul (Acts 19:33). The Jews put him forward to plead their cause before the mob.

places.name: Corinth
places.summary: A Grecian city, on the isthmus which joins the Peloponnesus to the mainland of Greece. It is about 48 miles west of Athens. The ancient city was destroyed by the Romans (B.C. 146), and that mentioned in the New Testament was quite a new city, having been rebuilt about a century afterwards and peopled by a colony of freedmen from Rome.

places.name: Ephesus
places.summary: The capital of proconsular Asia, which was the western part of Asia Minor. It was colonized principally from Athens. In the time of the Romans it bore the title of “the first and greatest metropolis of Asia.”

places.name: Asia
places.summary: Is used to denote Proconsular Asia, a Roman province which embraced the western parts of Asia Minor, and of which Ephesus was the capital, in Acts 2:9; 6:9; 16:6; 19:10, 22; 20:4, 16, 18, etc., and probably Asia Minor in Acts 19:26, 27; 21:27; 24:18; 27:2.

places.name: Achaia
places.summary: The name originally of a narrow strip of territory in Greece, on the north-west of the Peloponnesus. Subsequently it was applied by the Romans to the whole Peloponnesus, now called the Morea, and the south of Greece.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Macedonia
places.summary: In New Testament times, was a Roman province lying north of Greece. It was governed by a propraetor with the title of proconsul. Paul was summoned by the vision of the “man of Macedonia” to preach the gospel there (Acts 16:9).

places.name: Rome
places.summary: The most celebrated city in the world at the time of Christ. It is said to have been founded B.C. 753. When the New Testament was written, Rome was enriched and adorned with the spoils of the world, and contained a population estimated at 1,200,000, of which the half were slaves, and including representatives of nearly every nation then known.

events.title: Mission to Ephesus/1 Cor Written
events.summary: Passage: Acts 19:1–22. People: Erastus, Timotheus, Sceva, Tyrannus, Paul. Place: Asia, Ephesus.

events.title: Third Missionary Journey
events.summary: Passage: Acts 18:24–20:16. People: Paul, Luke, Timotheus, Aristarchus, Aquila, Priscilla and others. Lasted about 4 years.

events.title: Riot in Ephesus
events.summary: Passage: Acts 19:23–41. People: Alexander, Aristarchus, Gaius, Paul, Demetrius. Place: Asia, Ephesus.
